item.content:encoded:
I think I've now read through all of the HisCon entries, and I have commented on most of them. I was pleased to see a variety of approaches to the theme, although my sense was that not many of the entrants were inspired by the contest itself - there were a number of entries that were based on pre-existing works or ideas. Not that there is anything bad about that per se, but it suggests that a more specific topic might have produced a more creative response. However it may be that the wider scope led to the SCP entries being (on the whole) better-executed than the Tales, which is not usually the case.

My favourites:

Best SCP article: SCP-2498 by minmin. While it is very long, and it trades in some standard tropes, it commits absolutely to the idea, and feels a part of the pattern of history, rather than taking aim at a particularly well-known moment or individual. The character work is also well-served by its length, particularly in the relationships between characters.

Best Tale: What the Spybird Saw by Vezaz. A strong central idea rendered vividly and immediately, with some great turns of phrase.

Honourable mentions:

  • SCP-2736 by Hercules Rockefeller
  • SCP-2664 by A Random Day
  • Westbound and Down by Jekeled

WrongJohnSilver wrote his first article for the site as a contest entry back then, and now he's the author of many respectable and well-received articles for the site.

Just take your draft out for reviews on the Drafts Forum or site chat, take feedback from other members and improve based on feedback.

Even at worst, the article flops but you can learn from the experience as a whole to better yourself as a writer. No one will harp you for one failure.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
1. It's not against the rules, although I think that a story written about history as a concept goes against the spirit of the contest. We'll see what people come up with.

2. Anything historically significant, so stuff like the Arab Spring, the election of Obama, stuff in the recent past is okay. Just don't make your story about current events more than history and it should be fine.

3. The future is not history yet, so no. It has to be from the past.

4. You can make it anything you desire, as long as the historical context is there.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I have a few questions mostly having to do with the exact definition of history in this context.

1. Does history just mean historical events or can it also be history as a concept? An example would be something that could change history or create false history.

2. How far back does something have to be to count as a historical event? Does something that happened last year qualify?

3. Could we do future history as long as there is an emphasis on the history part? Like a "historical" event that hasn't happened yet?

4. If we do alternate history do we have to make it a major alteration? Like could it be about some minor fictional war that has no real bearing on modern life?

Sorry if these are a bit pedantic.
